case_number: Criminal Appeal No 118 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP(Crl) No 559 of 2022)
summary: Key issue: Whether criminal proceedings under Section 495 IPC against the appellant for concealing a prior marriage should be quashed. The Family Court had declared the divorce issued by the second respondent null and void and found that he failed to prove the appellant's prior subsisting marriage to Shoukat Ali. The prosecution alleges bigamy under Sections 494 and 495 IPC. The appellant argued that the Family Court’s binding finding bars relitigation and that criminal proceedings constitute abuse of process. The state contended that the issue requires trial. Relying on Neeharika Infrastructure, the Court emphasized that quashing is rare and only justified to prevent abuse of process or where no offence is disclosed. Despite conflicting findings, continuation of proceedings was not deemed an abuse given the seriousness of perjury allegations and public interest in prosecution. Outcome: Appeal dismissed; criminal proceedings allowed to continue.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Section 494 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
Section 495 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
Neeharika Infrastructure v. State of Maharashtra
Khawaja Nazir Ahmad v. King Emperor
final_judgment: Criminal Appeal dismissed. The stay on CR Case No 2512 of 2015 is vacated. The appellant shall face trial in the Court of SDJM(S) II, Kamrup (M), Guwahati.
